title: Lift finite-level presentation kernels to completed free kernel vectors
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal, B its I-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and T an inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system] annihilated at level n by I^(n+1), with surjective successor maps whose kernels are I^(n+1)T_(n+1). Let N be a B-module and e an A-linear isomorphism Res_A N to lim T satisfying the completed scalar residue equation [lem-weil-pbc-adic-tower-completed-scalar-limit]. Let d be a natural number and q a surjective B-linear map from the I-adic completion of A^d to N. If y maps to zero under q followed by the nth projection of e, there exists z with q(z)=0 and with the same evaluation in A^d/I^(n+1)A^d as y. No finiteness or Noetherian assumption is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 087W, proof: Lift finite-level presentation kernels to completed free kernel vectors

proof.text: Expand a completed free vector in the finite basis supplied by AdicCompletion.piEquivFin. Its coefficient evaluations are images of its free residue under the coordinate projections (AdicCompletion.map_val_apply), hence vanish when that residue vanishes. Apply the completed scalar residue equation with scalar representative zero to each basis summand. Thus each projected presentation vanishes on the free evaluation kernel.

For every j, reindex T by the cofinal shift k ↦ j+k. Mathlib Concrete.surjective_π_app_zero_of_surjective_map gives a surjective projection to T_j. Compose with the isomorphism e and the surjection q to obtain a surjective A-linear presentation p_j from the completed free module. The equations limit.w give compatibility of these presentations.

If p_j(x)=0, compatibility puts p_(j+1)(x) in the transition kernel I^(j+1)T_(j+1). Submodule.map_smul'' and surjectivity of p_(j+1) lift this image to w in I^(j+1) times the completed free module. Set x'=x-w. Then p_(j+1)(x')=0. Mathlib AdicCompletion.pow_smul_top_le_ker_eval shows eval_(j+1)(w)=0, so x' and x have the same preceding residue. This inclusion requires no finite generation of I.

Iterate this proved one-step correction starting with y: f_0=y and p_(n+k)(f_k)=0, while eval_(n+k+1)(f_(k+1))=eval_(n+k+1)(f_k). Classical choice here is applied only to a proved existence theorem. Applying transition maps and induction proves stabilization of every earlier residue.

Construct z directly as the completion element whose mth coordinate is eval_m(f_m). The stabilization equations and AdicCompletion.transitionMap_comp_eval_apply prove compatibility. They also give eval_(n+k+1)(z)=eval_(n+k+1)(f_k) for every k. Applying the first step to z-f_k gives p_(n+k)(z)=0.

For an arbitrary tower index j, map the zero coordinate at n+j down to j using limit.w. Thus every projection of e(q(z)) is zero. Concrete.limit_ext and injectivity of e.hom yield q(z)=0. The stabilized residue equation at k=0 gives the required nth residue equality with y.

lean.statement:
theorem adicTower_freeKernelCorrection (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (T : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ ModuleCat.{u} A)
    (hzero : ∀ n : ℕ, I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A (T.obj (op n))) = ⊥)
    (htrans : ∀ n : ℕ,
      Function.Surjective (T.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op) ∧
      LinearMap.ker (T.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op).hom =
        I ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule A (T.obj (op (n + 1)))))
    (N : ModuleCat.{u} (AdicCompletion I A))
    (e : (restrictScalars (algebraMap A (AdicCompletion I A))).obj N ≅ limit T)
    (hscalar : ∀ (n : ℕ) (r : AdicCompletion I A) (a : A) (x : N),
      AdicCompletion.evalₐ I (n + 1) r = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ (n + 1)) a →
      (e.hom ≫ limit.π T (op n)) (r • x) =
        a • (e.hom ≫ limit.π T (op n)) x)
    (d : ℕ) (q : AdicCompletion I (Fin d → A) →ₗ[AdicCompletion I A] N)
    (hq : Function.Surjective q) (n : ℕ) (y : AdicCompletion I (Fin d → A))
    (hy : (e.hom ≫ limit.π T (op n)) (q y) = 0) :
    ∃ z : AdicCompletion I (Fin d → A), q z = 0 ∧
      AdicCompletion.eval I (Fin d → A) (n + 1) z =
        AdicCompletion.eval I (Fin d → A) (n + 1) y
